title: A Ember for the Veil Revisited
premise: Emrys Kavanagh has spent her life as a temple scribe in the Veiled Valley, a sanctuary where magic cannot cross its borders—and where her own forbidden gift has stayed safely dormant. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley and she is exposed, Emrys flees into a world where her magic awakens violently, drawing her to the capital and to King Aldric, whose mind is slowly being consumed by the ancient entity bound inside his crown. With the help of a disgraced hunt-captain, a hedge-witch healer, and the king's estranged daughter, Emrys discovers the entity can only be unbound by a memory freely surrendered—someone must give up their most cherished recollection of love to sever it forever. In the climax, Emrys sacrifices her memories of her late mother's love to free Aldric, ending the hunt but leaving her hollow; in the end, her found family helps her rebuild new memories, proving that love outlives remembrance.
about_author: Dominic Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about duty, memory, and the quiet people history forgets, and live somewhere rainy with an ill-tempered cat.

chapters.title: Ink That Will Not Dry
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the Veiled Valley's temple scriptorium, scribe Emrys Kavanagh copies warding texts while hiding the strange warmth in her fingertips she's suppressed since childhood. A royal proclamation arrives: all gifted persons are to be registered—or hunted. Emotional beat: quiet dread settling over a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: The Valley Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys confides in Mother Sable, the temple elder who once smuggled gifted children across the border, and learns the valley's peace was bought with someone else's exile. Crown riders appear at the gates demanding entry. Emotional beat: the shattering of the illusion of safety.

chapters.title: What the Riders Bring
chapters.summary: POV Captain Ilsa Vane. Hunt-captain Ilsa Vane enters the valley under orders, disgusted by her commission, and senses something in the temple's youngest scribe. She delays the search by a day—a small mercy with large consequences. Emotional beat: conscience straining against duty.

chapters.title: The Night the Wards Failed
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The crown's hunters use a relic to pierce the valley's wards, and Emrys's gift flares involuntarily, saving a child from a collapsing beam—exposing her before the entire village. Ilsa looks away at the crucial moment. Emotional beat: terror, exposure, and an unexpected ally's silence.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Border
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Mother Sable gives Emrys a stolen travel pass and a warning: outside the valley, her gift will wake fully, and things will feel her waking. Emrys crosses the border alone at dawn. Emotional beat: grief for home mixed with the first thrill of freedom.

chapters.title: Everything Louder
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Beyond the veil, Emrys's magic erupts—she hears the land humming, sees threads of power everywhere, and accidentally heals a dying stranger in a roadside inn, drawing attention. A hedge-witch named Bree Ashdown finds her before the hunters do. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Kitchen
chapters.summary: POV Bree. Bree, exiled years ago for healing without license, takes Emrys in and teaches her basics of control. Through Bree, Emrys glimpses what a life outside the law could look like—warm, improvised, defiantly kind. Emotional beat: found family beginning to take root.

chapters.title: A Crown That Whispers
chapters.summary: POV King Aldric. In the capital, King Aldric fights nightly battles inside his own mind against the entity in his coronation crown, which engineered the witch-hunt to flush out strong gifts it can feed on. He is losing, and he knows it. Emotional beat: isolation of a man disappearing in plain sight.

chapters.title: Princess on the Staircase
chapters.summary: POV Princess Seraphine. Aldric's estranged daughter Seraphine notices her father speaking to empty rooms and burning letters addressed to old friends. Investigating, she finds her childhood nurse's name on the hunt registry—executed last month. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Fen Market
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Ilsa's hunters corner Emrys and Bree at the fen market, but Ilsa deliberately misdirects her squad, then confronts Emrys privately: she wants proof the king himself is compromised. Emotional beat: enemy becoming reluctant co-conspirator.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Temple
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Following clues in Mother Sable's parting letter, Emrys and Bree find a hidden archive revealing the crown-entity's origin: a starving god bound centuries ago by a queen who paid with her dearest memory. Emotional beat: awe and horror—the scale of the problem revealed.

chapters.title: An Audience Nobody Granted
chapters.summary: POV Seraphine. Seraphine smuggles Emrys into the palace disguised as her lady's maid after a coded letter proves Emrys knows what afflicts the king. Father and daughter meet again through the crisis, brittle and formal. Emotional beat: hope arriving in an unwelcome shape.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Face
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. The entity, sensing Emrys's proximity, seizes Aldric's body during council and nearly kills Seraphine when she resists its order to arrest the 'scribe.' Aldric claws back control long enough to beg Emrys for help. Emotional beat: horror and pity entwined.

chapters.title: Terms of Binding
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Studying the archive with Seraphine and Bree, Emrys learns the unbinding rite requires a freely given memory of profound love—but every attempt historically killed the giver. Ilsa arrives with news: the Grand Huntress is coming to purge the palace itself. Emotional beat: the cost made explicit.

chapters.title: What We Keep, What We Give
chapters.summary: POV Bree. Bree volunteers her own memory of her lost wife, arguing her life is already half-spent; Emrys refuses to let her. The group argues through the night about sacrifice, love, and who gets to decide. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened into conflict.

chapters.title: The Grand Huntress Comes
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The Grand Huntress Maren Voss arrives, suspicious of Ilsa's reports, and orders the palace sealed. Ilsa burns her commission papers and joins the conspirators openly, buying them hours with a forged quarantine decree. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Siege of Quiet Rooms
chapters.summary: POV Seraphine. As Voss's hunters sweep the palace, Seraphine leads Emrys through servant passages toward the throne room, fighting past her own guardsmen, some of whom choose to look away. Emotional beat: courage discovered in ordinary people.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the throne room, Emrys begins the rite as the entity unleashes Aldric's stolen power against them. Bree holds the circle, Ilsa holds the door, Seraphine holds her father's hand. Emotional beat: desperate, collaborative climax.

chapters.title: A Memory Freely Given
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At the rite's crux, Bree falters—and Emrys offers instead her deepest memory: her mother singing to her in the temple garden. The entity, offered true love freely given, cannot refuse the terms and unravels. Emotional beat: devastating triumph.

chapters.title: The Hollow Morning
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. Freed but broken, Aldric abdicates in favor of Seraphine and dissolves the hunt. Emrys wakes with a hole where her mother used to be, unable to grieve someone she cannot remember. Emotional beat: victory's terrible price.

chapters.title: Rebuilding From Ash
chapters.summary: POV Bree. Bree tends Emrys through the numb aftermath, telling her stories of the mother she no longer recalls until Emrys can weep. Ilsa, Seraphine, and Bree formally become her household. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes bearable.

chapters.title: New Ink, Old Garden
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Months later, Emrys returns to the valley to see Mother Sable, then chooses to leave again—not fleeing, but belonging to two homes. She begins writing a book of her own, planting a garden like the one she forgot. Emotional beat: peace earned, love remembered without remembering.
